documents.t: Worked examples — executed notebooks rendered as pages (refreshed weekly against the live APIs): Quickstart
Hand-written wrappers, loaders, and helpers in sportsdataverse.hockey.shl that are not generated API-endpoint wrappers (those have their own reference pages).

shl_player_crosswalk(season: 'int', game_type: 'str' = 'regular', *, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'Frame' isa player id -> athlete uuid for every player of an SHL season, from one stats-info call. The SHL has three player id systems: the isa (StatNet) id that play-by-play, box scores and stats tables key on, the platform athlete uuid that rosters and athlete routes key on, and the old ramses_legacy CMS id (athlete-details only). The players_summary table's players{} map is keyed by isa and carries each player's uuid, skaters and goalies alike. Parameters Returns polars.DataFrame | pandas.DataFrame: one row per player: player_id (isa, Int64), athlete_uuid (Utf8; null where SHL has none, common before about 2005), first_name, last_name, full_name, date_of_birth (YYYY-MM-DD), nationality, gender, position, shoots, ep_url (all Utf8), jersey_number, weight (kg) and height (cm) (Int64). Raises Example from sportsdataverse.hockey.shl import shl_player_crosswalk xw = shl_player_crosswalk(2026) xw.filter(xw["player_id"] == 2427)

shl_ssgt_uuid(season: 'int', game_type: 'str' = 'regular') -> 'str' The SHL ssgt uuid of a season (END year) and game type, from /statistics-v2/layout-info. Use it for the routes that take an ssgt uuid directly (shl_standings, shl_sites, shl_ssgt_provider, shl_post_game_team_stats, shl_player_h2h). The directory is fetched once per process. Parameters Returns the ssgt uuid (e.g. "iuzqg7dqk9" for the 2025/26 regular season). Raises Example from sportsdataverse.hockey.shl import shl_ssgt_uuid shl_ssgt_uuid(2026) # 2025/26 regular season shl_ssgt_uuid(2025, "playoff")

return_parsed=True (default) — a tidy polars.DataFrame with the columns below; pass return_as_pandas=True for a pandas.DataFrame. return_parsed=False — the raw JSON Dict payload, unparsed.
